goal: Train real LanM LoRA adapters for both Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B, then compare base/trained and thinking off/on using the same frozen LanM evaluation/runtime.

proposed_training.precision: QLoRA4 for both sizes, bf16 compute
proposed_training.trained_parameters: Language LoRA only; no vision, embeddings, LM head, or DeltaNet-specific projections
proposed_training.loss: Assistant answer and tool-call tokens with EOS; all prompt/tool observations and empty thinking prefixes masked

limitations: Official Unsloth Qwen3.5 guidance recommends bf16 LoRA over 4-bit due to quantization differences. Published bf16 estimates are about 10GB for 4B and22GB for9B; these are vendor estimates, not measurements on this laptop.
This is supervised direct-answer/tool-use adaptation, not reasoning-trace training or new scientific validation.
The paper corpus contains duplicate formats and structured evidence; it is not itself a ready supervised training set.
Existing Unsloth GGUF provenance identifies the official Qwen base but does not record its original weights revision. Matching exact base lineage requires verification or disclosure.
data_policy: Curated training-only records under local-training/data, with separate groups and provenance. Exclude benchmark prompts, fixtures, expected answers, rubrics, results, model outputs, current chat transcripts and live project IDs.
validation: CPU token mask test using official chat template
Record exact token counts and no truncation
Held-out loss before and after one epoch
Nonzero learned LoRA B matrices and adapter hashes
CPU adapter conversion using llama.cpp b12323 source
Real adapter load and tool smoke using the same benchmark llama.cpp binary
Frozen behavioral benchmark for trained vs base under both thinking settings
isolation: Models, datasets, checkpoints, adapters, logs, exports and provenance remain within local-training. A task-specific persistent WSL dependency/build-cache environment at /var/tmp/lanm-training-20261118 avoids Windows filesystem latency and tmpfs cleanup; its exact executable and packages are recorded in environment.json and environment-lock.txt. No global configuration changes. GPU training waits for coordinator release.
